hints.title: Use consecutive pairs
hints.body: In the recurrence, the input is the current term and the output is the next term. Use the transitions from the first term to the second and from the second to the third.
hints.recap: Each observed transition gives an equation involving the same two constants.
hints.pitfall: Do not substitute the term number where the term value belongs.
hints.pause: Write the two equations for the unknown constants.

recall.reminder: A recurrence specifies how a new term is calculated from an earlier term.

hints.title: Turn the fractions into linear equations
hints.body: For the first transition, 5(3+q)=3+p. Construct the corresponding equation for the next transition, then subtract to eliminate one unknown.
hints.recap: Clearing the two denominators exposes a simultaneous linear system.
hints.pitfall: Keep the multiplier attached to every term inside each bracket.
hints.pause: Solve for both constants and check the two observed transitions.

recall.reminder: Elimination is especially efficient when the same unknown has the same coefficient in both equations.

hints.title: Advance from the third term
hints.body: Once the constants are known, put the third term into the recurrence: x4=(7+p)/(7+q).
hints.recap: The next step uses the last known term and the original rule.
hints.pitfall: Check that the new denominator is nonzero before evaluating.
hints.pause: Insert your constants and simplify the resulting fraction.

recall.reminder: Evaluate each recurrence step using the term already obtained, keeping the original indexing.

solution:
The transitions 3→5 and 5→7 give 5(3+q)=3+p and 7(5+q)=5+p. These simplify to p−5q=12 and p−7q=30.

Subtracting gives q=−9, then p=−33. Thus the fourth term is 7−337−9=13. The denominators used for the first three transitions are −6,−4,−2, all nonzero. Answer H.
knowledgePattern: Two transitions determine the two constants in a rational recurrence
